subject: Access evidence request: SSO/SCIM/RBAC package for ClearLoop pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <security@clearloop.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@clearloop.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access evidence request: SSO/SCIM/RBAC artifacts for ClearLoop pilot

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the pilot meeting last week. As part of our security intake for evaluation and internal compliance, we need a compact package of IAM artifacts to validate integration and least-privilege controls before progressing to procurement. Could you share the following sample artifacts and short notes?

- Redacted SAML assertion samples (NameID, attributes, signature block preserved)
- SCIM provisioning/Delta export for a 7-day window (timestamps, actor, delta type)
- Role entitlement snapshot and owner roster (mapping of service roles to human owners)
- Service account runbook excerpt (creation, rotation, and usage justification)
- A brief note on RBAC enforcement (how we prevent privilege creep; automated checks if any)
- Data retention policy for auth logs and SCIM deltas

This can be redacted for PII; we just need enough to validate traceability and least-privilege controls. Our deadline for the initial evidence bundle is Fri Sep 10 if possible — we will follow with a short SOC/SIG questionnaire after this.

Also confirm whether the artifacts will be tenant-scoped or global (we're evaluating multi-tenant isolation).

Appreciate a quick ACK and rough ETA.

-Jordan
Security Lead, ClearLoop
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <security@clearloop.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access evidence request: SSO/SCIM/RBAC artifacts for ClearLoop pilot

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Laid out below is our proposed approach and attachments to kick this off.

What we'll do now:
- Share an initial checklist and short summary (attached) that maps your ask to deliverables.
- Provide redacted SAML assertions and a SCIM delta sample from a staging tenant first (to preserve production PII).
- Deliver a role-owner matrix and a short runbook snippet showing service-account rotation.

Attachments: redwood_iam_evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx, iam-ask-summary.pdf

Timeline (provisional):
- Staging samples & short notes: 3 business days
- Full package (including runbook extract and role roster): 10–12 business days

Question: are you ok receiving staging samples first and then a production-sanitized package? Also, are you expecting tenant-scoped artifacts (per-customer) or a single global snapshot — we can provide both but want to size the effort.

I'll loop in Laura (IAM leads) and Mina (Access governance) for delivery. If you prefer, we can do a 30-min walkthrough to annotate the artifacts as we hand them over: https://cal.com/redwood/30min

Best,
Karthik
Director, Customer Security Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <security@clearloop.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access evidence request: SSO/SCIM/RBAC artifacts for ClearLoop pilot

Jordan — looping in the delivery plan and specifics so you have clarity on content and redaction approach.

Short answers up front:
- Tenant scoping: we can produce per-tenant SCIM deltas and SAML samples for the pilot tenant.
- Redaction: we will preserve assertion structure (NameID, attributes, issuer, timestamps, signature) and redact PII values (e.g., email -> [redacted@example.com]).
- RBAC/least-privilege: we'll include the entitlement snapshot plus a short note on automated expiration policies and periodic owner certification cadence.

Delivery breakdown:
1) Day 0 (today): checklist & summary (attached) — confirms ask mapping.
2) Day 1–3: Staging SAML assertion example (saml-assertion-example-redacted.xml), SCIM delta sample for a 7-day window (scim-delta-sample.csv), brief README with field definitions.
3) Day 4–10: Role-owner matrix (CSV), runbook excerpt for service-account lifecycle (PDF), retention policy excerpt, and evidence of periodic owner recertification.

Notes on scope and constraints:
- For production SCIM exports we will need a signed request from your security contact and a brief SPI (signed processing instruction) to allow export of production logs — this is standard for customer data access.
- We will not publish full private keys or unredacted user emails; auditability will be preserved via traces (actor ids, timestamps, change types).

Attachments to this message: saml-assertion-example-redacted.xml, scim-delta-sample.csv

If that plan works, we'll queue the staging artifacts and schedule the walkthrough to annotate the SAML/SCIM fields with your team.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura — that breakdown is perfect. Staging samples first is fine; we just need enough context to validate the integration and our procurement team has requested a contact for export approvals and a procurement POC for the contract timeline. Can you provide the security contact name/email we'll use for the SPI and a procurement contact?

Also: quick ask — can you include a one-paragraph summary of how Redwood enforces least privilege for tenant-scoped roles? Procurement often wants that in the contract addendum.

-Jordan
